payload.pattern: A surface that declares it is maintained is making a CLAIM, not reporting a fact. Grep for its WRITER before trusting it. payload.context: Found from ATLAS (nested-web-root monorepo, type=app) while running check-canon-conformance.mjs --project . --offline. Three independent defects in studio-ops instrumentation each convert a conformant project into a reported STRONG-tier canon GAP or error. All reproductions below were run live from the ATLAS repo on 2026-08-17; none is inferred from reading code alone.

defects.problem: findField() returns a value only when `typeof obj[field] === "number"`. Any CANON_MATRIX entry whose passIf declares a BOOLEAN can therefore never be read: findField returns undefined and line 72 reports status "error" with detail "could not read <field> from checker output". This is portfolio-wide, not ATLAS-specific — every project with a boolean-passIf canon is silently unmeasurable.
reproduce: # CANON-045 row => {"conformance":"error","detail":"could not read pass from checker output","exit":0}
defects.actual: CANON-045 reported as error, counted against the project.
defects.suggestedFix: Accept booleans (and arguably strings) in findField, not only numbers. Note line 74 already handles eq correctly (v === eq), so findField is the sole blocker. Consider failing LOUD on a passIf whose field exists but has an unsupported type, rather than degrading to "error" — the two are indistinguishable to a reader today.

defects.problem: Checker stdout is parsed as JSON.parse(out.split("\n").pop()) — only the LAST LINE. Checkers that pretty-print their JSON (check-dual-audience.mjs and check-stats-surface.mjs both do, via JSON.stringify(..., null, 2)) fail to parse, so `parsed` is null and the detail fallback on line 77 emits the last line sliced to 90 chars — literally "}". The gap is reported; the REASON for it is destroyed, which is the half a human needs.
defects.suggestedFix: Parse the whole stdout first and fall back to last-line only if that fails; or require single-line JSON from checkers and lint it. Either way a detail of "}" should be treated as a parse failure and reported as such, never rendered to a human as a reason.

defects.problem: Both checkers resolve artifact candidates relative to the project root and enumerate only FLAT repo layouts (agents.json | public/agents.json | static/… | dist/…; stats/index.html | src/pages/stats.* | app/stats/page.* | index.html | …). A project whose web root is nested — ATLAS ships from ATLAS_v0.8_Windows_Safe_Export/ATLAS_v08/atlas/apps/web/, its declared build authority — has every artifact reported null and receives two phantom STRONG-tier canon GAPs. check-stats-surface.mjs already warns in its own source (lines 225-228) that an artifact "somewhere unusual would be a checker bug wearing a canon badge". That is this case.
evidence: Artifacts that DO exist and ship in ATLAS:
Note the CANON-054 DESCRIPTOR half resolves fine (context/STATS_SURFACE.json, metrics 8, analyzed 8, showcase 4) — only the page/homepage location probe is blind.
defects.suggestedFix: Let a project declare its web root once — a registry field (e.g. webRoot) or a repo-local descriptor — and resolve all artifact candidates beneath it, falling back to the current flat list. Critically: when NO candidate matches anywhere, distinguish "searched and absent" from "could not locate the web root at all". Today they collapse into the same GAP, which is what makes the false negative invisible.

payload.crossCuttingLesson: All three defects share one shape: an instrument reports a confident verdict about something it never successfully measured. A boolean it cannot read becomes "error"; JSON it cannot parse becomes a reason of "}"; a directory it cannot find becomes "missing". In every case UNMEASURED is rendered as MEASURED-AND-BAD. The generalisable fix is to make unmeasured a first-class, visibly distinct outcome in the conformance runner — never silently folded into gap/error.
payload.atlasHandling: ATLAS did NOT patch the sibling tree (CANON-018; studio-ops also holds an active session lock). It shipped this cargo and added an independent local checker (scripts/check-nested-web-root-canon.mjs, 11 tests incl. proven reds) that verifies the CANON-048/054 artifacts at the real nested web root, so ATLAS holds a truthful verdict without silencing or overriding the control-plane checkers. payload.headline: Three session-start instruments were rendering UNMEASURED as MEASURED-AND-BAD; all three fixed or truthfully re-measured.
impact: Doctor score: the brief's refresh had a 30s deadline against >240s of work and timed out on EVERY render (receipt: deadline-exceeded 30137ms), hidden by stdio:ignore + non-fatal handling. Worse, the refresher was not the field's writer — status.doctorScore is written only by bounded-closeout-doctor.mjs, while the preflight spawned the 188-probe control-plane doctor. Now the row renders provenance ("N/M cached Xh old (reason) - not measured now", sigil ⚠) and the refresh defers to its owner at closeout. Default brief render: 250s → 18s.

Freshness gate: lib/brief-semantic-fingerprint.mjs had ZERO importers, so check-brief-staleness.mjs returned semantic-fingerprint-missing unconditionally and could never exit 0 — a gate that was wired, permanently red, and therefore ignored. Emitting the marker exposed two structurally dead inputs (a regex matching only parenthesised handoff headings; a `generatedAt` key the test cache never writes).

Canon gaps: CANON-048/054 GAPs were checker path-blindness against a nested web root where the artifacts exist and ship; CANON-045 reported "could not read pass" while its checker returns {"pass":true} exit 0.
transferableLessons: Before wiring anything to refresh a field, find who WRITES it. A refresher that is not the field's writer can only time out or overwrite with a foreign shape — and it will do so silently if the spawn is non-fatal with stdio ignored.

When rendering a cached value to a human, render its provenance with it. Reserve ✓/⛔ for in-band measurements and use ⚠ for "could not measure". Unknown must fail closed as unrefreshed, never as fresh.

A guard that turns green after a fix must be proven able to go RED for EACH input it claims to watch. Two of five inputs here were structurally null; emitting the marker alone would have produced a confident green gate blind to the two inputs most likely to change.

A bounded deadline is fine; a bounded deadline that hides its own exhaustion is not. If the work legitimately exceeds any sane render-time budget, that is an architecture signal, not a number to raise.

When a local fix must diverge from a propagated module, print the control plane's verdict verbatim and NAME the divergence. A wrapper that reclassifies a sibling's red without showing it is how a red becomes a silent green.

payload.solution: If the same party supplies both sides of a comparison, the check is a tautology. TLP S308: Proof-of-Life verified an Ed25519 signature with a public key the caller sent in the same request, and compared the fingerprint to a hash of that same key - so any session-token holder could mint a throwaway keypair and produce unbroken verified liveness under the primitive gating inheritance. Fix: bind acceptance to STORED enrolled state (key epochs), and keep historical validity separate from live acceptance so legitimate key rotation does not void history.
payload.pattern: A verification is only worth what its inputs are worth
